If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3–5 days, increase forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to compensate for pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply (±0.33) in the last 3 days, apply a 0.5–1.5% asymmetric correction to the forecast peak, favoring the direction of the most recent sentiment.  
For late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67), apply a 0.5% smoothing decay to forecast values to reduce volatility.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is trending downward, reverse the last 2–3 forecast points to align with sentiment momentum.  
If sentiment is negative but forecast is trending upward, reduce the last 2–3 forecast points by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment drag.
